How long before the adhan the island shows a heads-up.
Show the island over other apps
The island is a small black pill at your camera that shows the next prayer, and opens into a card when you tap it.
To draw over other apps, Android asks for the permission “Display over other apps”. Ufuq uses it for the island and nothing else.
Ufuq does not read what is on your screen and has no internet access.
You can turn it off any time in Settings. The Live Update chip shows the same countdown without this permission, and is the best choice with a screen reader.
Rides, deliveries and timers from apps you choose. Off by default.
Only the apps you tick below show here.
Needs notification access to see ongoing notifications.
None yet. An app appears here after it shows a ride, delivery, timer or progress notification.
Show other apps in the island
Ufuq reads the title and progress of ongoing notifications, such as a ride, a delivery, a timer or a download, from the apps you choose.
It does not read messages, chats or any other notification, and ignores apps you have not chosen, media (shown separately) and calls.
Nothing is stored or sent. Ufuq has no internet access and keeps only the list of apps you chose.
This uses Android’s notification access, the same permission the media page needs. After you grant it, tick the apps to show in Settings. You can turn it off any time.
Do Not Disturb for a few minutes after each adhan, then back to how it was. Off by default.
Needs Do Not Disturb access. Tap to set it up.
Android is not allowing exact alarms, so silence may start a few minutes late.
Silence while you are within 100 m of a saved mosque, and restore when you leave.
Adding a mosque needs precise location.
Optional. Lets Android tell Ufuq you reached a mosque while the app is closed.
Could not get your location. Try again outdoors.
After each adhan, Ufuq turns on Do Not Disturb for the time you choose, then puts your phone back exactly as it was.
Android keeps this behind a special permission, “Do Not Disturb access”. Ufuq uses it only to switch Do Not Disturb on and off for this.
If you had Do Not Disturb on yourself, Ufuq leaves it alone. If you change it during the silence, Ufuq steps aside. Alarms are never blocked.
Reach a mosque while the app is closed
Saved mosques work by watching for you coming within 100 m. For this to work when Ufuq is not open, Android needs “Allow all the time” location.

Ufuq only compares your position with the places you saved. It has no internet access, and nothing leaves your phone. Without it, saved mosques only work while Ufuq is open; the timed silence after each adhan works either way.
Shows when sahur ends (Subuh) and counts down to iftar (Maghrib), with a progress bar. It also turns on by itself during Ramadan.
After you move 25 km or more, Ufuq updates the city and time zone. Coarse location, no internet.
A quiet notice when prayer times move with you.
